items.title: SBTi seeks more input on net-zero electricity rules
items.summary: The Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) is asking for feedback on potential changes to the electricity criteria included in its revised corporate net-zero standard.

items.title: How Lenovo uses product carbon footprints to sell refurbished tech
items.summary: Lenovo is the global leader in unit sales of both new and refurbished notebook and personal computers, commanding estimated market shares of 27 percent and 18 percent, respectively.

items.title: Preparing your business for the future cost of EV charging
items.summary: Last year, 70% of the world's leading corporate fleets did not add a single new petrol or diesel vehicle, according to the Climate Group.

items.title: COP31: Businesses and banks back Global Electrification Pledge to usher in ‘age of electricity’
items.summary: The COP31 Presidency’s landmark pledge to usher in the “age of electricity” by increasing the share of final energy demand met by electricity has been backed by more than 180 companies and financial institutions, while utility organisations have committed more than $150bn annually to the scheme.

items.title: Oil and gas majors double down on expansion despite transition pledges
items.summary: New data from Urgewald revealed that expansion plans persist for fossil fuel firms despite climate concerns and uncertainty surrounding long-term demand.

items.title: Pension funds face 30% hit to returns by 2050 in 2.8C world
items.summary: With global warming potentially heading to a 3C increase, new analysis has predicted 30% of pension fund returns could be at risk by mid-century.

items.title: IEA predicts 4,800GW of renewables to be added through 2031
items.summary: Global renewable energy capacity is set to increase by almost 5,000 gigawatts (GW) by 2031, with emerging and developing economies outside China matching advanced economies for new installations for the first time.
